solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rattle off, reportedly on location getting place elsewhere

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to rattle off a list is to recite it; said aloud it matches the answer
RE means on or concerning
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Someone reels off details while out on location, as a film crew decides to set up somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: Two routes lead to RESITE: it sounds like RECITE, and it is also RE (on) plus SITE (location).
explanation.definitionFit: To resite something is to move it to a new position, literally to site it again.

clue.text: Rescued judge in long grass

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
to deem is to judge or consider

explanation.surface: A judge rescued after getting lost in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem is to save or deliver, so redeemed means rescued, as from sin or captivity.

clue.text: A month in Tel Aviv? End of June quiet mostly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the last letter of June
a lull is a quiet period

explanation.surface: Wondering about a month in Israel: by the end of June things go quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: Tel Aviv stands for Jewish usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Elul is the sixth month of the Jewish civil calendar, around August and September, so a month as reckoned in Israel.

clue.text: Factory whose past is shocking

indicators.note: something shocking is disordered and upsetting, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A factory with a disgraceful history.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is &lit-flavoured: a sweatshop is exactly a factory with a shocking past.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a workplace, typically a factory, where workers are paid little for long hours.

clue.text: Bond has time for new driver Pat

indicators.note: having one thing for another means a swap, and a new driver displays an L-plate, so that letter is the one replaced

blocks.note: a league is a bond or alliance
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: James Bond makes time for a new driver called Pat.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, the new driver, and T takes its place. Pat is a traditional nickname for an Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Teague is a dated nickname for an Irishman, as Pat or Paddy is.

clue.text: Dog starts to sniff heels nastily biting one? Sue!

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept
biting means taking something between the teeth, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the first letters of the three words
I is the Roman numeral for one
Sue Barker is a former British tennis player and TV sports presenter

explanation.surface: A nasty dog sniffs and nips at someone's heels, and the victim wonders about suing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue!' looks like legal action; it is the first name of Sue Barker, giving the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A shinbarker is a contemptuous term for a small yapping dog, one that barks at people's shins.

clue.text: Result from past Highland cattle

blocks.note: PA is an abbreviation for past, as in past participle
nout is a Scots word for cattle

explanation.surface: A farming outcome arising from Highland cattle in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highland' does not describe the breed; it marks the word for cattle as Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan out is to turn out or end up, so to result, from gold-panning yielding a find.

clue.text: Old South American concerned with extremes in Colombia

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: to be in something is to be concerned with it, as in 'in insurance'
the first and last letters of Colombia

explanation.surface: A historical note about an ancient South American with links to Colombia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca people ruled a great empire in the Andes before the Spanish conquest, so an Inca is an old South American.

clue.text: Reveal Scotch and unopened brandy

indicators.note: unopened means without its opening, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: bingo is old slang for brandy

explanation.surface: A bottle of Scotch whisky and an unopened bottle of brandy are revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky; it labels the word as Scottish. A reveal is the side surface of a door or window opening.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots an ingo is the reveal of a door or window, the inner side face of the opening.

clue.text: Chasing minister in Corsica about island railway

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the others

blocks.note: a curé is a French parish priest, and Corsica is French
IS is the abbreviation for island
EL is the American elevated railway

explanation.surface: Pursuing a Corsican clergyman around an island railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' reads as pursuit; it is the craft of chasing metal, decorating it by engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciselure is the art of chasing, ornamenting metal by engraving or embossing, and also work done that way.

clue.text: Lawyer in short is clever, escaping term in prison

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so the final letter of the word is the one taken
something escaping gets away, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: natty means neat and deft, so clever
the last letter of prison

explanation.surface: A short but smart lawyer who escaped a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term in prison' looks like a sentence; term means end, the last letter of prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Atty is the standard abbreviation for attorney, a lawyer.

clue.text: Grace, Elizabeth and Harry meeting Italian

blocks.note: Bet is a pet form of Elizabeth
Harry and Hank are both familiar forms of Henry
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: Royals Elizabeth and Harry being introduced to an Italian with grace and charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace looks like an adjective-style compliment to the royals, but it is a prayer before a meal; BETHANKIT is the Scots grace, from 'be thankit'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a bethankit is a short prayer of thanks said at table, which is exactly what a grace is.

clue.text: After changing limits, made application for subscription

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters, and changing them means swapping the two ends round

blocks.note: to sue is to make an application to a court

explanation.surface: Someone who applied after altering the terms, perhaps for club membership.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the S and D at the two ends of SUED to get DUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dues are the regular fees a member pays, the same thing as a membership subscription.

clue.text: Money for the bar concerning new students

blocks.note: RE means concerning
freshers are first-year students in British universities

explanation.surface: Drinks money for the pub, on behalf of new students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; it means barristers collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher is an extra fee paid to a barrister for each day a case continues, so money for the legal bar.

clue.text: Swallow nesting afresh, bottom of garden abandoned

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so that letter is dropped from the word
doing something afresh means starting over in a new way, so the letters are rearranged
'bottom of' keeps only the last letter of 'garden'

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of garden

explanation.surface: A swallow building a new nest, having given up on the bottom of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' pretends to be the bird nesting in the garden; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest food is to take it into the body by mouth, which is to swallow it.

clue.text: Libya's high-ranking officer gets increase

blocks.note: LAR is Libya's international vehicle registration code
GEN is the abbreviation for general

explanation.surface: A top Libyan military officer receives a pay rise or promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Largen is an old or poetic verb meaning to make or grow larger, so to increase.

clue.text: Con artist nervous about the army

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery and unsettled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A fraudster getting jittery over the military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about the army' is the definition read as an adjective phrase, of or concerning the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratonic means relating to an army, from Greek stratos, an army; the definition is an adjectival phrase.

clue.text: Amphibians once again focus on crossings

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is kept

blocks.note: EFT is an obsolete adverb meaning again
the central letter of crossings

explanation.surface: Newts and frogs returning yet again to the same road crossings, a familiar sight in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' flags that the sense of again is archaic, not that something happens one time.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, especially a young one, and newts are amphibians.

clue.text: Fixed in fine voice, abnormally high one

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: F for fine plus alto, a voice
set means fixed

explanation.surface: A singer stuck with an unusually high voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abnormally high one' refers back to 'voice', a register above the natural one.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a man's artificially high singing voice above his normal range.

clue.text: Serve behind edges of line

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outer letters, so only the first and last are kept

blocks.note: a butt is the backside or behind
the first and last letters of line

explanation.surface: A tennis instruction to serve from behind the edge of the baseline.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTTLE is a jocular back-formation from butler.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttle is to act as a butler, which means waiting on people and serving them.

clue.text: Needn't do running as a continuous sequence

indicators.note: running suggests things moving about, so the letters are set in motion into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone excused from jogging all the way without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: End to end means one after another with no gaps, so in an unbroken series.

clue.text: Rank bad meal starter, final directions ignored

indicators.note: the last letters of the two words are both compass-style directions, left and right, and ignoring them means leaving them out
something bad has gone wrong, so the letters come out in a spoiled order

blocks.note: meal without its final letter
starter without its final letter

explanation.surface: A restaurant review: the opening course of the meal was terrible, and the final instructions were disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of meal and starter are L and R, abbreviations for left and right, so both are ignored before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterate is the degree or status of a master, an academic rank.

clue.text: Disheartened guide tense over getting back

indicators.note: losing heart here means losing one of the middle letters of the word
in a down-or-across clue 'over' asks for the word to be turned over and read the other way

blocks.note: to steer is to guide
a drawn face looks tense

explanation.surface: A dispirited, nervous guide on the way back from a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like a grammar term beside 'Disheartened'; it means strained, as a drawn face is. Losing heart here removes just one of the two middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternward means towards the stern or rear of a ship, so back as an adverb of direction.

clue.text: Head of tasting approves sweet wines

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of tasting
to okay something is to approve it

explanation.surface: The chief taster gives the thumbs-up to some dessert wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine from the Tokaj region.

clue.text: Flag up in new area gastropods with round shells

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular genus name

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top
in places one word inside another

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
to flag is to tire
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A flag is raised over a new area where round-shelled snails live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner going up; it is the verb, to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerita is a genus of sea snails, gastropod molluscs with rounded, globular shells.

clue.text: Medic sharing military awards in form of crosses

indicators.note: sharing a space means sitting inside it, so one word is put within the other

blocks.note: the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration
MO is medical officer

explanation.surface: An army doctor sharing military medals, which happen to be shaped like crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The DSO medal is itself a cross, so 'crosses' looks like a description of the awards; it means hybrid animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A dsomo is a hybrid of a yak and a domestic cow, so dsomos are crossbred animals, crosses.

clue.text: Don't change from road with central area blocked off

indicators.note: blocking off the central area of the word cuts out its two middle letters

blocks.note: a street is a road

explanation.surface: A planning objection: leave this road alone, even with its middle closed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The two central letters of STREET, R and E, are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand, telling the typesetter not to alter the text.

clue.text: East German or Italian? No answer

indicators.note: having no answer means the letter abbreviating answer is taken away

blocks.note: ossia is the Italian word for or, used in music for an alternative passage

explanation.surface: A question of nationality: is someone East German or Italian, with no reply given.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the abbreviation for answer, dropped from the end of OSSIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossi is the informal German term for a person from the former East Germany.

clue.text: Lady not entirely shining in retreat

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter short of the whole word, so the last letter goes
retreating means going backwards, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: aglow means shining

explanation.surface: A lady whose glow fades as she withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a woman's first name, so a lady in the crossword sense of a female name.

clue.text: Historically fine man a great success

blocks.note: a man is a he
a show that is a riot is a great success

explanation.surface: A handsome man from the past who was a huge hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine man' reads as a compliment, but 'fine' belongs to the definition as a noun, a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A heriot was a feudal payment due to a lord when a tenant died, so historically a kind of fine.

clue.text: Port item subject to inflation

blocks.note: first meaning: an ancient Phoenician port in Lebanon
second meaning: a rubber wheel covering that is pumped up with air

explanation.surface: A harbour town where prices keep rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' suggests rising prices; it is air being pumped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre is a city in Lebanon on the Mediterranean, and a tyre is an inflatable wheel covering.

clue.text: Freak least attached to ecstasy tablets

indicators.note: a freak is an abnormal outcome, so the letters come out in an unnatural order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A warning about a strange reaction to even the smallest number of ecstasy pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstasy tablets' looks like a single phrase about pills; the tablets are stone slabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stelae are upright stone slabs bearing inscriptions, a sense of tablets as carved stones.

clue.text: Canadian channel is close by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by sound means the words are to be heard, not spelt

blocks.note: is contracted to 's, plus nigh, meaning close

explanation.surface: A Canadian TV channel that seems to be closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests television; it is a watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Canada a snye is a side channel of a river, a natural water channel.

clue.text: Macedonian affected by liturgy

blocks.note: stagy means theatrical, affected
a rite is a liturgical form of service

explanation.surface: An Orthodox Macedonian deeply moved by the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected by' reads as emotionally moved; here it is the word stagy followed by its partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was born in Stagira in Macedonia and is called the Stagirite, so a Stagyrite is a Macedonian from that town.

clue.text: Northern tourist destination in conservation area

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A popular northern holiday spot set within a protected landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island in the Scottish Hebrides, famous for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona, off the west coast of Scotland, draws many visitors and pilgrims, so it is a northern tourist destination.

clue.text: Opened church in the country

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: a land is a country
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A new church officially opened somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened' suggests a ceremony; it means cut open, as a doctor does a boil.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance a boil is to pierce it with a blade, so lanced means cut open.
